FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Feelings & Kindness flashcards.

Thirty-five cards, four words each: the feelings a four-year-old lives with, the kind habits that make days gentler and the calm-down skills that turn big feelings into words. Show the card, say the words together, try the real thing — that is the whole method, and it works.

These cards belong to Class 38 · Feelings & Kindness on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name the faces first

    Hold the card where your child can see the four panels and read each word aloud. Point to the face that matches — the smile, the frown, the fists, the closed eyes — then let your child point and name them back to you.

  2. 02

    Say the words together

    Every card page has a "Say it together" script in parent words. Say it naturally, make the faces with them, and let whatever they answer be the right answer — a word, a face, a giggle all count.

  3. 03

    Practise the real thing

    The card is the rehearsal; the breakfast table, the playground and bedtime are the show. Each card page has a "Try this" idea for using the words on a real moment the same day.

  4. 04

    One card a sitting is plenty

    Pick the card that fits your family this week — mornings? sharing? the big-feelings days? — and let it live on the fridge. Thirty-five cards is a whole term of five-minute feelings talks.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Happy, Sad, Angry & Calm Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four feelings a four-year-old meets every single day, on one card: happy, sad, angry and calm — each one a face they will recognise from the mirror.

      Say it together

      “Happy looks like this! Sad looks like this. Angry looks like this — eyebrows down! And calm… slow breath, soft face. Can you make all four faces with me?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play the four-faces game: you name a feeling, your child makes the face. Then swap — they name, you make the face (an exaggerated grown-up angry face gets the biggest laughs). End by finding the feeling right now: "Which one are you today?"

      Quick parent note

      Naming a feeling is the first step to taming it — a child who can say "I am angry" already has one foot back in calm. Four words, one card, the start of the whole class.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Happy, Sad, Angry & Calm lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Kind, Share, Help & Thank You Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The first four kind words, each shown by a child actually doing it: a kind heart, a shared book, a helping hand and a thank you said with clasped hands.

      Say it together

      “Heart friendly, book handed over, small friend helped up and a big warm thank you — four kind words your child can say AND do before lunch.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Catch the words in the wild today: "You SHARED your crackers — that was kind!" "Thank you for HELPING me." Naming the act the moment it happens teaches the word faster than any drill.

      Quick parent note

      Kindness words arrive in pairs with the acts themselves — say the word while the doing is still happening and the two stick together for good.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Kind, Share, Help & Thank You lesson on the Learning Path.

      Excited, Worried, Surprised & Proud Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A huge grin, some anxious eyebrows, a round surprised O and a tall crossed-arms smile — four bigger feelings, four very different faces.

      Say it together

      “Excited is when your body goes wiggle-wiggle! Worried is when your tummy feels tight. Surprised is when your mouth goes OH. And proud is when you stand tall like this.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Act all four with the whole body: wiggle for excited, hug your own arms for worried, jump-back-OH for surprised, tall-stack for proud. Then hunt them in a book: "Find the surprised face!"

      Quick parent note

      Bodies feel feelings before words do — acting them out gives your child a way to notice what is happening inside and hang the right word on it.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Excited, Worried, Surprised & Proud lesson on the Learning Path.

      Listen, Gentle, Take Turns & Kind Words Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A hand cupped to an ear, arms wrapped tenderly, a patient raised finger and a warm talking smile — the four playtime habits, drawn gently.

      Say it together

      “Listen means ears open, mouth waiting. Gentle means soft hands with people and pets. Take turns means my go, then your go. Kind words are words that make friends feel good.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practise each one in a minute: listen to one whole song, stroke the pet (or a soft toy) gently, take three turns rolling a ball, and say one kind word each at dinner.

      Quick parent note

      These four are playground currency — children who can listen, be gentle, take turns and speak kindly get included again and again, and inclusion is where more kindness grows.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Listen, Gentle, Take Turns & Kind Words lesson on the Learning Path.

      Breathe, Brave, Try Again & I Can Do It Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Hands folded mid-breath, a little cape with a fist in the air, a determined second fist and a small confident nod — the courage ladder at child size.

      Say it together

      “First we breathe — in like a flower, out like a candle. Then we think brave. Then we try again. And we say it together: I can do it.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Pick one wobbly thing today — a big slide, a new food, a tricky puzzle — and walk the ladder out loud: breathe, brave, try again, I can do it. Cheering allowed and encouraged.

      Quick parent note

      Courage is a sequence, not a personality trait — breathe first, brave second, try third. Children who learn the steps stop waiting to feel brave and start doing brave instead.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Breathe, Brave, Try Again & I Can Do It lesson on the Learning Path.

      Smile, Care, Forgive & Friend Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A boy beams, a girl hugs a pink heart, another boy folds his hands peacefully and a fourth waves hello — the friendship ladder, panel by panel.

      Say it together

      “A smile says hello, I am friendly. Care means I notice when you are sad. Forgive means we start again after a fight. And a friend is someone we smile at, care for and forgive.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play the mend-it game with toys: two puppets squabble, one says sorry, the other says "I forgive you" — then they play again. Children rehearse mending long before they need it for real.

      Quick parent note

      Friendship is not the absence of fights — it is the presence of repair. Forgive is the word that turns a broken moment back into a friendship, and it is learnable at four.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Smile, Care, Forgive & Friend lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Lonely, Loved, Frustrated & Relaxed Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Four deeper feelings every preschooler knows but cannot always name: the ache of lonely, the warmth of loved, the hot push of frustrated and the slow ease of relaxed.

      Say it together

      “Lonely is when you want someone and they are not there. Loved is when someone holds you close. Frustrated is when it will not work and you want to yell. Relaxed is when your whole body goes soft.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Sort today into the four boxes at bedtime: "When did you feel lonely? When did you feel loved? What frustrated you? What made you relaxed?" No fixing, just naming — the naming is the lesson.

      Quick parent note

      Lonely and frustrated are the two feelings that most often come out as behaviour — a child with the words for them needs far fewer meltdowns to say the same thing.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Lonely, Loved, Frustrated & Relaxed lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Patient, Honest, Polite & Fair Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Closed eyes waiting calmly, a hand on a heart, folded polite hands and a thinking-about-fairness frown — four character words at four-year-old size.

      Say it together

      “Patient means I can wait. Honest means I tell the truth, even about the broken cup. Polite means please, thank you, excuse me. Fair means everybody gets a turn — including the little ones.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play a waiting game (patience), ask a question with an honest answer built in ("did you like the broccoli?"), practise one polite phrase, then deal cards one-each (fair) — four minutes, four words.

      Quick parent note

      Fair is the word four-year-olds police hardest — "that is not FAIR" is the first moral protest. Give them the word and the rule together and the protests become negotiations.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Patient, Honest, Polite & Fair lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Notice, Understand, Comfort & Encourage Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four empathy steps in child-size order: notice the feeling, understand it, comfort the friend and encourage the next try.

      Say it together

      “First we notice — "your face looks sad." Then we understand — "are you sad because the tower fell?" Then we comfort — a hug, a hand, a sit-together. Then we encourage — "try again, I will help."”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Walk the four steps on a real moment: a dropped ice cream, a lost toy, a friend who fell over. Your child plays all four parts — spotter, understander, comforter, cheerleader.

      Quick parent note

      Empathy is a skill with steps, not a mood children either have or lack. Name the steps and any four-year-old can run them — most just need someone to show the order.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Notice, Understand, Comfort & Encourage lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Wait, Ask, Listen Carefully & Say Sorry Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Still hands, a raised hand, an ear cupped close and an apology ready — the four moves that keep a playdate kind from start to finish.

      Say it together

      “Wait — I do not grab. Ask — "may I have a turn?" Listen carefully — ears on, eyes on. And when I get it wrong, I say sorry and mean it.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Rehearse the ask: hide a favourite toy, then have the grown-up want it back — your child practises wait, ask, and hand it over with a smile. Swap roles and let them be the asker.

      Quick parent note

      Sorry lands better when it is modelled, not forced — say sorry to your child when you snap or forget, and the word becomes a real repair tool instead of a punishment password.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Wait, Ask, Listen Carefully & Say Sorry lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Welcome, Include, Cooperate & Teamwork Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four group words every classroom runs on: welcome the newcomer, include the left-out one, cooperate on the task and feel the teamwork when it works.

      Say it together

      “Welcome means "hi, come in!" Include means "you can play too." Cooperate means we each do a part. Teamwork is what it feels like when we do it together.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Build something that needs four hands — a sofa-cushion fort, a puzzle, a snack plate arranged together. Say the words while it happens: "I welcome you… I include you… we cooperate… TEAMWORK!"

      Quick parent note

      The child who says "you can play too" is doing the single most pro-social thing an early-years classroom can teach — inclusion is kindness with its sleeves rolled up.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Welcome, Include, Cooperate & Teamwork lesson on the Learning Path.

      Hopeful, Safe, Problem Solver & Kind Heart Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A bright upward cheer, a content closed-eyes smile, a boy planning over his notebook and a girl hugging a big heart — strong days, drawn from the inside.

      Say it together

      “Hopeful means I believe good things are coming. Safe means nothing here can hurt me. Problem solver means when something goes wrong, I look for a fix. Kind heart means all of it runs on kindness.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Do the problem-solver pose: hands on hips, "something went wrong — what could we TRY?" List two silly fixes and one real one. Then name the kind heart that did it: "you just solved that with kindness."

      Quick parent note

      Hope and safety are the soil every other skill grows in — a child who feels safe tries more, and a child who tries more has more chances to watch their own kind heart work.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Hopeful, Safe, Problem Solver & Kind Heart lesson on the Learning Path.

      Joyful, Tired, Confused & Curious Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four feelings of a full day: the arm-throwing joy, the yawning tired, the scratching-head confused and the finger-to-chin curious.

      Say it together

      “Joyful is happy with your WHOLE body. Tired is when a yawn sneaks out. Confused is when you do not get it yet. Curious is when you want to know more.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Do the day-in-four at dinner: act joyful, droop tired, shrug confused, lean-in curious — matching each to a real moment from the day. The acting is the vocabulary lesson.

      Quick parent note

      Confused and curious are the same face one second apart — teaching both words together shows your child that not-knowing is just curiosity that has not started yet.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Joyful, Tired, Confused & Curious lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Scared, Brave, Shy & Confident Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Worried hands near a face, fists ready for anything, a girl peeking from behind her hair and a proud crossed-arms smile — courage drawn honestly, all four speeds.

      Say it together

      “Scared is when you want to hide. Brave is when you do it anyway. Shy is when new people make you quiet. Confident is when you stand tall and try.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw the feeling map: which things are scary, which are shy-things, which feel confident? Grown-up fills one in too ("phone calls make me shy!") — honesty about fear is the lesson.

      Quick parent note

      Brave is not the opposite of scared — it is scared that went ahead anyway. And shy is not a flaw to fix, just a warming-up speed to respect. Say both out loud.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Scared, Brave, Shy & Confident lesson on the Learning Path.

      Share, Give, Care & Thank Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Two children and one teddy, a gift changing hands, a grown-up hugging a small child close and a boy with both hands on his heart — giving in all its shapes.

      Say it together

      “Share means we both use it. Give means here, it is yours now. Care means I keep you warm and safe. Thank means I saw what you did — and it mattered.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Run one tiny giving circle today: share a snack between plates, give one toy to the donation bag, care for a tired teddy, thank whoever helped. Four words, four real acts, five minutes.

      Quick parent note

      Giving has more than one shape — a child who hates sharing a favourite toy may love giving a drawing or caring for a baby sibling. All four count; the card says so.

      Teach it, step by step

      Be Kind, Helpful, Patient & Honest Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four be-words — values turned into things a four-year-old can actually do: be kind, be helpful, be patient and be honest.

      Say it together

      “Be kind — soft hands, warm words. Be helpful — see a job, do a job. Be patient — wait without wailing. Be honest — tell it true, even the wobbly parts.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Give the be-words jobs: one kindness mission, one helper job (match the socks), one waiting moment (timer for the oven), one honest report ("who spilled it?" — telling true earns a cheer, not a trouble).

      Quick parent note

      "Be" words work because they name the child, not just the act — "you WERE patient" becomes who they are. Four little identity seeds, planted five minutes at a time.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Be Kind, Helpful, Patient & Honest lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Forgive, Accept, Respect & Include Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four deeper friendship words: forgive repairs the past, accept lets people be different, respect treats every one as valuable and include opens the circle.

      Say it together

      “Forgive means we start fresh. Accept means you can be you and I can be me. Respect means I treat you like you matter. Include means I make room for you — always.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play the open-circle game: a toy crowd plays "everyone can join" — the circle literally opens wider each time someone is included. Then practise the words: "I forgive you. I accept you. I respect you. Come in!"

      Quick parent note

      These are the words that make groups kind — a classroom of four-year-olds who can forgive, accept, respect and include runs itself almost. Start with one word a week.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Forgive, Accept, Respect & Include lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Pause, Breathe Deeply, Think & Choose Kindness Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four-step pause that fits between a feeling and a reaction: pause, breathe deeply, think and then — the child gets to choose kindness.

      Say it together

      “Pause — freeze like a statue. Breathe deeply — in through the nose, out slow. Think — what is happening? Then the big one: choose kindness.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Freeze-dance with a twist: when the music stops, everyone pauses, takes one deep breath, thinks "how do I feel?" and picks one kind thing to do next round. The pause becomes a habit their body knows.

      Quick parent note

      The pause is the whole trick of self-regulation in four words — between the spark and the flame there is a gap, and a four-year-old who can pause there owns the moment instead of it owning them.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pause, Breathe Deeply, Think & Choose Kindness lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Proud, Disappointed, Grateful & Peaceful Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The wins-and-setbacks feelings: the tall smile of proud, the drooped shoulders of disappointed, the warm thanks of grateful and the settled slow of peaceful.

      Say it together

      “Show me your proudest tower-walk! Now your droopiest disappointed face… and your softest peaceful one. Grateful hands go on your heart — there it is.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Share one proud and one disappointing moment each at dinner — grown-ups go first, honestly. End with one grateful thing and one peaceful minute of quiet breathing together.

      Quick parent note

      Practised on rained-off park trips and sold-out cookies, the disappointed word grows the muscle your child will need for much bigger days later on.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Proud, Disappointed, Grateful & Peaceful lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Worried, Relieved, Jealous & Embarrassed Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four tricky feelings everyone has and nobody puts on the wall: worried, relieved, jealous and embarrassed — named here so no child carries them unnamed.

      Say it together

      “Let us play the four faces: worried mouth… relieved phew! Jealous fists… embarrassed blush. Which one visited you today — and which one can you make RIGHT NOW?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Tell one grown-up story for each: a worry that turned out fine (relieved!), a jealous moment, an embarrassing one — told lightly, laughed with, not at. Your honesty gives them permission.

      Quick parent note

      Jealous and embarrassed are the loneliest feelings in preschool — simply hearing "everyone feels that, even grown-ups" takes half the weight off a small chest.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Worried, Relieved, Jealous & Embarrassed lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Notice, Name, Share Feelings & Ask for Help Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A boy raises his hand mid-notice, a girl names it with a finger to her chin, a boy shares with an open palm and a girl gets ready to ask — the whole check-in on one card.

      Say it together

      “First notice: "something is happening in my chest." Then name it: "I think it is worried." Then share it: "I feel worried." And if it is too big: "Can you help me?"”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Build the check-in into the day — at breakfast and bedtime, everyone (grown-ups too) runs the four steps in one sentence: "I notice… I feel… I share… I need…"

      Quick parent note

      The whole class funnelled into one habit: a feeling that gets noticed, named and shared almost never has to come out as a tantrum. Ask-for-help is the safety net under all of it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Say Hello, Make Space, Be Curious & Ask Nicely Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four joining-in words: hello to open the door, make-space to save a seat, be-curious to find out about someone and ask-nicely to get things gently.

      Say it together

      “Say hello — big or small, it counts. Make space — scoot over, there is room. Be curious — "what do you like?" Ask nicely — "may I?" works better than grabbing, every time.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practise on toys first: two stuffed animals meet, one says hello, the other makes space on the bench, they get curious about each other and ask nicely for the crayons. Then try it for real at the park.

      Quick parent note

      Most preschool friendships start with someone making space — literally. A child who can scoot over and say hello owns the single most useful social skill there is.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Say Hello, Make Space, Be Curious & Ask Nicely lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Share the Space, Work Together, Take Turns & Cheer Others Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four playdate words: share the space when it gets crowded, work together on the big build, take turns with the good parts and cheer others when they shine.

      Say it together

      “Scoot in — there is room! Hold it, I will stack it. My go… your go… and when she lands the big one: YAY, you did it!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Build a block tower with a rule: only one block each, then pass — sharing space, working together, taking turns in one game. Every wobble gets a cheer from the whole family.

      Quick parent note

      The thumbs-up for somebody else’s win is the hardest and best habit on the card — it is jealousy’s opposite, learned at carpet-time scale.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Share the Space, Work Together, Take Turns & Cheer Others lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Kind Choice, Good Friend, Try Your Best & Grow Together Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four growing words: every kind choice plants something, a good friend waters it, try-your-best gives it sun and grow-together is the harvest.

      Say it together

      “Kind choice — I picked kind, even when it was hard. Good friend — I showed up for someone. Try your best — not perfect, just my all. Grow together — we get bigger side by side.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Name the moments backwards at bedtime: "what was today’s kind choice? who was a good friend? what did you try your best at?" Then one grow-together plan for tomorrow.

      Quick parent note

      Growth language ("try your best", "grow together") beats cleverness language ("so smart") in every study that compares them — this card hands your family the words.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Kind Choice, Good Friend, Try Your Best & Grow Together lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Calm Down, Count to Ten, Use Your Words & Take a Break Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four real calm-down moves, for the stormy moments: calm the body, count the breath, say the words and — when all else fails — take a break.

      Say it together

      “Slow body… count the fingers, one to ten… now the words: I am angry because… Still stormy? Break time — the cushion is always there.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Make the calm-down corner real before it is needed: a cushion, one book, one soft toy. Practise visiting it on a HAPPY day so the place feels friendly, not like exile.

      Quick parent note

      Calm-down skills are the emergency services of the feelings world — drilled on quiet days so they work on loud ones. Every step on this card can be rehearsed when nothing is wrong.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Calm Down, Count to Ten, Use Your Words & Take a Break lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      I Feel, I Need, I Want & I Choose Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Four children, four sentences that start with I: one thinking her feeling, one explaining his need, one saying his want plainly, one owning her choice.

      Say it together

      “I feel… sad. I need… a hug. I want… the blue cup. I choose… the puzzle. Four sentences that start with I — because your feelings and your wishes are yours to say.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play the I-statement dinner game: everyone says one sentence starting with each word — I feel, I need, I want, I choose. Grown-ups include one real one ("I need five quiet minutes!").

      Quick parent note

      The same wish that used to come out as grabbing or whining now arrives as a sentence — four calm starters, said with I, heard the first time.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the I Feel, I Need, I Want & I Choose lesson on the Learning Path.

      Listen First, Think First, Speak Kindly & Solve Together Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four steps for settling any squabble: listen first, think first, speak kindly and solve it together — the order matters, and the card keeps it.

      Say it together

      “Listen first — both sides, no interrupting. Think first — before the words come out. Speak kindly — even if you are right. Solve together — the fix both people can live with.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Mediate the next toy dispute with the four steps spoken out loud — you narrate, they do: "listen… now think… say it kindly… what is the together-fix?" Step back a little more each time.

      Quick parent note

      Conflict is not the enemy of friendship — unhandled conflict is. These four steps turn squabbles into practice, and a child who can solve together at four negotiates for life.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Listen First, Think First, Speak Kindly & Solve Together lesson on the Learning Path.

      Welcome All, Be Inclusive, Share Joy & Make a Friend Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four open-door words: welcome all comers, be inclusive on purpose, share the joy out loud and make a friend — maybe the day’s best achievement.

      Say it together

      “Welcome all — everyone gets a hello. Be inclusive — nobody plays alone unless they want to. Share joy — happiness grows when it is given away. Make a friend — today is a good day for it.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Pick one inclusion mission: at the park or preschool today, be the one who says hello to someone new or invites the standing-alone child in. Debrief at dinner — how did it feel?

      Quick parent note

      The child who walks toward the standing-alone one is doing the hardest, bravest kind of kindness — and it gets easier every single time it is tried.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Welcome All, Be Inclusive, Share Joy & Make a Friend lesson on the Learning Path.

      You Matter, I Am Here, You Are Safe & We Care Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four sentences every child needs to hear — and, in time, to say back: you matter, I am here, you are safe and we care.

      Say it together

      “You matter — exactly as you are. I am here — right beside you. You are safe — this minute is okay. We care — the whole family, all together.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Say all four on a hard day — a fall, a nightmare, a goodbye at the door. Then teach them as comfort-words your child can offer: to a friend who skinned a knee, to a baby who cried, to you.

      Quick parent note

      Reassurance works best when it is rhythmical and repeated — the same four sentences on the hard days become the voice a child eventually carries inside their own head.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the You Matter, I Am Here, You Are Safe & We Care lesson on the Learning Path.

      Keep Trying, Learn, Celebrate & Be Yourself Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four confidence words for beginners and finishers alike: keep trying through the wobbles, learn from every go, celebrate every win and be yourself the whole time.

      Say it together

      “Keep trying — wobbles are part of it. Learn — every try teaches something. Celebrate — the small wins too! Be yourself — there is only one you, and that is the good news.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Hold a family celebration for one thing that was HARD today — confetti optional, cheering mandatory. Name the keep-trying part out loud so the effort is the hero, not just the result.

      Quick parent note

      The wins that get noticed are the wins that get repeated — five seconds of cheering buys another week of trying.

      Teach it, step by step

      Welcome, Belong, Trust & Connect Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A wave at the door, hands folded contentedly, a palm resting on a heart and arms reaching out — the four beams a family house stands on.

      Say it together

      “Welcome — you are wanted here. Belong — this is your spot, your cup, your people. Trust — I keep my word to you. Connect — we check in, we laugh, we are us.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Find the belonging evidence together: your coat hook, your cup, your seat in the car, your bedtime song. Belonging is built out of small fixed things — point to each one and name it theirs.

      Quick parent note

      Belonging is not a feeling that appears — it is built from hooks with names on them, kept promises and bedtime rituals. This card names the four beams so your child can see the house.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Welcome, Belong, Trust & Connect lesson on the Learning Path.

      Notice, Pause, Breathe & Reset Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four-step reset button for a moment going sideways: notice it is happening, pause the action, breathe the storm smaller and reset the moment.

      Say it together

      “Notice — "uh oh, a big feeling is coming." Pause — everything stops. Breathe — one slow breath in, one slow breath out. Reset — "okay, let us start this bit again."”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play reset-tag: when someone (grown-up included) notices the play tipping over, they shout RESET — everyone freezes, one breath together, then the game restarts fresh. Grown-ups calling RESET on themselves is the best demo there is.

      Quick parent note

      Reset gives families a word that stops a spiral without blame — nobody is in trouble, the moment just starts again. That single move saves afternoons.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Notice, Pause, Breathe & Reset lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Feelings & Kindness (Class 38) class on the Learning Path.

      Care, Support, Encourage & Comfort Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four helping words for when someone needs you: care that notices, support that carries a corner, encourage that cheers the next try and comfort that sits close.

      Say it together

      “Care — I see you are having a hard time. Support — I will hold part of it. Encourage — "you have got this." Comfort — a hug, a blanket, me, right here.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Care for the caregiver: when a grown-up has a hard day, let your child run all four — notice it, help carry something, cheer you up, deliver the hug. Children give care brilliantly when invited.

      Quick parent note

      Children who are trusted with real caring jobs — comforting, encouraging, supporting — build empathy faster than any lecture could teach it. The card is the invitation.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Care, Support, Encourage & Comfort lesson on the Learning Path.

      Listen, Understand, Respond & Forgive Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The four conversation words that mend and grow friendships: listen all the way, understand before answering, respond with care and forgive when it wobbles.

      Say it together

      “Listen — all the way to the end. Understand — "so you felt left out?" Respond — "here is what I think." Forgive — "we are okay, let us play."”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Hold a two-minute listening date: one person talks about their day, the other may not interrupt, then must say back one thing they heard. Swap. Even three-year-olds can do the "one thing I heard" part.

      Quick parent note

      Most preschool conflicts are two people talking and nobody listening — this card teaches the order that fixes it: ears first, heart second, mouth third, forgiveness always.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Listen, Understand, Respond & Forgive lesson on the Learning Path.

      Kind Words, Kind Actions, Kind Heart & Choose Kindness Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A girl speaks her kindness, a boy offers his hand, another boy holds a heart and two children hug — the four layers of kindness, drawn in one frame.

      Say it together

      “Kind words — we say nice things. Kind actions — we do helpful things. Kind heart — we feel for people. Choose kindness — nobody makes us; we pick it. Every time, we get to pick it.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Kindness hunt: spot one kind word, one kind action and one kind heart in your day — then ask the big question: "what kindness will YOU choose tomorrow?" Answer in the morning.

      Quick parent note

      The last lesson of the class is also its first: kindness is a choice, repeated until it looks like a personality. Thirty-five cards later, your child holds a whole vocabulary of feelings-and-kindness words — and the picking.
